s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent syncope with transient complete atrioventricular block
salient_findings: Gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction
key_facts: Patient in their late 40s
Admitted for uterine myomectomy procedure
No history of structural heart disease
No history of hypertension, myocarditis, or sleep apnea syndrome
No family history of cardiovascular disease and sudden death
No pharmacologic agents affecting cardiac rhythm
Normal laboratory tests
Normal initial 12-lead ECG
Normal chest radiographic imaging
Normal echocardiographic findings
Holter monitor recording showed ventricular asystole during syncope
Electrophysiologic studies showed no abnormalities in the cardiac conduction system

shortlist.label: Paroxysmal complete atrioventricular block
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced ventricular asystole during syncope with gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction followed by complete atrioventricular block

shortlist.label: Vagus-mediated paroxysmal atrioventricular block
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and Holter monitor recording are consistent with vagus-mediated paroxysmal atrioventricular block

shortlist.label: Neurally mediated syncope
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and normal laboratory tests are consistent with neurally mediated syncope

shortlist.label: Vasovagal syncope
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and normal electrophysiologic studies are consistent with vasovagal syncope

shortlist.label: Idiopathic complete atrioventricular block
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has no history of structural heart disease and normal electrophysiologic studies, making idiopathic complete atrioventricular block a possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's Holter monitor recording showed a 23.8-second ventricular asystole during syncope with gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction, which is consistent with vagus-mediated paroxysmal atrioventricular block.

rejected.label: Paroxysmal complete atrioventricular block
rejected.why: Lack of underlying structural heart disease

rejected.label: Neurally mediated syncope
rejected.why: The presence of ventricular asystole during syncope suggests a more specific cardiac conduction disorder

rejected.label: Vasovagal syncope
rejected.why: The term 'vasovagal' typically implies a specific trigger, such as pain or stress, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Idiopathic complete atrioventricular block
rejected.why: The term 'idiopathic' implies an unknown cause, but the vagus-mediated mechanism is suggested by the gradual slowing of the sinus rate and atrioventricular conduction
